description: OpenTitan UART F5 behavior (the sticky tx_done event, INTR_STATE word and one-write W1C clear) plus one framed serial peer on the device's own rx/tx/tx_en pins, driven and sampled by the host at a declared bit period.
notes: the F5 facts are configs/behaviors/opentitan_uart_tx_done_f5.json's, with one deliberate difference: CTRL(16) is 0x80000003 instead of 0xffff0001, so the declared bit period is exactly 32 host ticks in both directions. The 16x baud tick comes from the NCO: uart_core.sv:164-177 increments a 17-bit accumulator by ctrl.nco on every cycle while tx_enable or rx_enable, and tick_baud_x16 is its carry. With nco=0x8000 the carry fires every second cycle, so one bit (16 such ticks) is 32 cycles; a bit_ticks declaration of 32 is that arithmetic, not a measurement

CTRL bits (uart.hjson): 0 TX enable, 1 RX enable, 6 PARITY_EN, 7 PARITY_ODD, 31:16 NCO. 0x80000003 therefore enables both directions at NCO=0x8000; the receiver has to be enabled for the peer's frame to be accepted, and the transmitter for the F5 tx_done event to fire

trigger_writes: INTR_ENABLE(4)=4 unmasks tx_done (INTR_STATE bit 2); CTRL(16)=0x80000003 enables TX and RX at the declared baud; WDATA(28)=0x5a pushes the one byte the transmitter serializes. tx_done is an Event source, so it sets INTR_STATE bit 2 and stays set until 1 is written to it

the serial peer: rx_role 'rx' is the profile's uart.pins input the host drives, tx_role 'tx' is its output the host samples, tx_en_role 'tx_en' is the device's own transmit-enable output the host samples but never drives. idle_level 1 is the UART line's idle level and frame 8n1 is one start bit, eight data bits LSB first and one stop bit

the peer drives a complete frame only for a case whose record carries a stimulus byte (the F2 record's optional second word); the CPU clock is parked while the frame is on the wire, so the device has the byte before the CPU reads its data register. With no stimulus word the peer only samples the device's tx line
no execution is claimed by this file: the run under runs/p2-pins-serial-20261103/ is the evidence
